before.existing_compacted_memory: Settlements at N41 (O5, Wh9, B10) and N14 (Wh8, W3, W4). Immediate Goal: Build settlement at N7 Brick Port (B2); road is complete. Hand: 2W, 2Wh, 1S, 2O. Missing: 1 Brick. Strategic Context: Alice is a close ally; we have maintained a mutual anti-Bob front. Bob is hostile and his primary Brick source (B6) is blocked by the robber. I have repeatedly refused Bob's 3:1 Wheat-for-Wood offers to prevent his expansion. Alice attempted to trade for my Wood, but I am holding all materials for the N7 build. Plan: Maintain robber on B6 to starve Bob of Brick while I secure the port. Need a 6 or 10 roll, or a trade with Alice for Brick.

relevant_chat.message: Glad you stuck to your guns, Charlie. Bob's 'generosity' usually comes with a steep price tag later. Let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling.
Charlie, you still looking for wheat after that 8? I've got some to spare if you can part with a bit of wood. Let's keep the momentum going.

I'd love to help you out, Alice, especially since we've been working well together, but I'm still clutching that wood for my own settlement plans. If I let it go now, I'll be stuck waiting on the dice even longer.
No worries, Charlie. I get the 'settlement fever'—it's hard to let go of the pieces when you're that close. I'll just hold tight for now and see what the next roll brings.
Alright, let's see if those dice feel like helping me out with some building supplies. Everyone's talking about that robber, but I'm just looking for a good roll here.

Since nobody seems to have any brick to spare with that robber sitting on the 6, I guess I'll see what the development deck has in store for me. Maybe there's a knight in there who's tired of seeing Bob's hex blocked.
A knight would be a welcome sight, Charlie. That robber has definitely overstayed his welcome on the brick.
A 3... not exactly the spark I was looking for. I'm going to hold onto my cards for now and see what the next round brings. Your turn, Alice.
Since the brick situation is so dire with that robber, I think I'll follow your lead, Charlie, and see if the development deck has anything helpful. We really need to get things moving again.
Smart move, Alice. Hopefully you pull a Knight so we can keep managing that robber together.
I figured you’d be eager to move that, Bob. Just don't get too comfortable with wherever you're putting it.
Sorry Charlie, but you've been a bit too successful with those wood rolls lately. I need to balance the scales a little.
You make me sound like a villain, Alice! I'm just trying to keep the economy moving. But hey, a 5 is a start.
Alright, let's see if we can get those dice to cooperate. Everyone's looking a bit too comfortable with that robber sitting on my brick.
That robber on the 6 is really putting a damper on things. If anyone's tired of seeing that grey piece, I'm happy to help move it if I can get some materials.
Alright, let's see if we can get something going. Hopefully the dice are kinder than that robber has been.

Eleven... well, that doesn't help any of us, does it? It's quiet out here with that robber still hogging the brickworks. I think I'll just pass the dice and hope for a more productive round next time.
Alright, let's see if we can get those dice to cooperate. Everyone's looking a bit too comfortable with that robber sitting on my brick, but maybe a good roll will change the conversation.
Well, look at that. Seven. I think that grey piece has spent quite enough time on my brick, don't you? Let's see how you two like having your wheat fields shared with a guest for a change.
Spoken like a true 'community' leader, Bob. Always looking for ways to share the burden.
